Subject: Technical deep dive recap: latency & throughput SLOs for Acme POC

Hi Samantha / Michael, thanks for the productive session this morning. Quick recap of what we covered, confirmed pain points, and recommended next steps. Attaching the SLO matrix and a deployment diagram (see attachments).

1) Pain points you described - inconsistent p95/p99 latency during peak windows (spikes tied to concurrent user submissions and certain long-context queries) - surprising token cost increases as query volume grows - occasional request timeouts during batch heavy periods

2) Goals for the POC (as discussed) - Target p95 latency: <= 120 ms for typical generation workloads (avg response ~180 tokens) - Target p99 latency: <= 400 ms for production traffic - Sustained throughput target: 200 requests/sec from the gateway; peak burst capacity up to 500 req/sec for short windows - Cost objective: keep per-request token cost within X% of current baseline (we'll confirm the exact percent once you share sample billing)

3) Model & request profile - Preferred model family: Llama 3 class (13B quantized for inference) for the initial POC due to cost/perf balance; we discussed fallback to a smaller q4_0 variant during extremely high load - Context length required: up to 8k tokens for RAG use cases; average request token count observed in samples: ~180 tokens; some outliers up to ~1.2k tokens - Need for deterministic outputs for ranking: we recommend temperature <= 0.3 and a consistent sampling policy during evaluation

4) Recommended deployment topology (POC) - Environment: Redwood Hosted + Dedicated capacity feeler - run inference on a dedicated pool in us-west for low-latency routing; optional Private deployment later for full isolation - Serving runtime config: continuous batching with workload-aware batch sizing, KV-cache for repeated prefix contexts, and per-route batching windows (20-40ms) to balance latency and throughput - Autoscaling: policy for sustained target 200 rps with burst buffer to 500 rps; configure scale-down cooldown to avoid flapping during short bursts - Fallback & routing: smart routing policy to route by latency SLO; automatic fallback to quantized smaller model when queue depth exceeds threshold - Networking: recommend egress IP allowlist (we'll provide the range) and minimal TLS termination latency by colocating gateway in us-west

5) Implementation notes & tradeoffs - Quantization: q4_0 or q4_k_mt provide strong perf for 13B models; we can benchmark both and provide kernel-level latency numbers - Batching windows vs latency: increasing batching windows improves throughput but adds tail latency - we suggested target windows of 20ms for p95-driven workloads - Memory: 13B q4 will require ~10-12 GB GPU memory per replica with KV-cache overhead; plan for autoscaling nodes with at least 48GB GPU memory for safety on longer contexts

6) Action items / next steps - Acme: share sample query set and 48-hour traffic trace (owner: Samantha) - due 2026-06-18 - Redwood: run initial latency/cost micro-benchmarks for 13B q4_0 vs q4_k_mt and share numbers (owner: Ethan) - target 2026-06-19 - Redwood: provide dedicated pool sizing recommendation and a draft mutual action plan for the POC (owner: Marissa) - target 2026-06-20 - Both: schedule a follow-up to review benchmark results and confirm POC config (owner: Laura) - proposed week of 6/22

Please see the attached acme-slo-matrix.xlsx and redwood-deployment-diagram.png for the numeric targets and a simple topology diagram. Also linking the HubSpot record here for reference: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/AcmeCorp

Questions / clarifications: you mentioned a requirement to preserve query ordering for some ranking flows - can you confirm whether strict ordering is required end-to-end or if eventual ordering (on the application layer) is acceptable? Also, please confirm whether the PII controls for the dataset require on-prem handling.

Thanks again - looking forward to the next steps.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the recap - a few technical clarifications from the infra side: 

- Sequence lengths & memory: for the 8k context case with 13B q4_0 we should budget ~12-14GB GPU memory per active replica when KV cache is warm. If you expect >8k frequently we should consider 32GB-class GPUs or context offload.
- Tokenization & batching: average 180 tokens/request is what we used in our bucketed sizing; to hit 200 rps with 20ms batching windows we recommend a competitive batcher that adapts by request size.
- Concurrency: plan for a request concurrency target of ~6-12 in-flight requests per replica depending on avg tokens. This will influence total replica count.
- Benchmarks: I'll run q4_0 vs q4_k_mt on our perf harness (same model weights) and include p50/p95/p99 latencies and cost estimates per 1k requests. Expect results by EOD 6/19.

Action: Ethan -> run benchmarks (6/19), Marissa -> draft sizing and MAP (6/20), Samantha -> data & allowlist (6/18).

Onwards - happy to jump on a quick sync if you want to walk through the perf charts.


Ethan
